'''Hocine Haciane Constantin'''{{family name footnote|lang=Catalan|Haciane|Constantin}} (born 7 July 1986 in [[Andorra la Vella]])<ref>{{cite Sports-Reference |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ha/hocine-haciane-1.html |access-date=2013-06-13 |title=Archived copy |archive-date=7 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121107145107/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ha/hocine-haciane-1.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> is an Olympic and [[List of Andorran records in swimming|national record]] holding [[swimmer]] from [[Andorra]].<ref>[http://www.andorra2005.ad/seguiment/articles/detall.aspx?IdArticle=72&IdIdioma=en Haciane wins the final of the 200 metres]  {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070928082754/http://www.andorra2005.ad/seguiment/articles/detall.aspx?IdArticle=72&IdIdioma=en |date=28 September 2007 }}</ref>  At the 2004 Olympics, he was [[List of flag bearers for Andorra at the Olympics|Andorra's flagbearer]].<ref>[http://www.smh.com.au/olympics/schedule/swimming/day5.html Day 5 Swimming Schedule & Results]  {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060526171236/http://www.smh.com.au/olympics/schedule/swimming/day5.html |date=26 May 2006 }}</ref>

He has swum for Andorra at the:
*Olympics: [[Andorra at the 2004 Summer Olympics|2004]],<ref>2004 Olympics results: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040820055656/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/olympics/2004/schedules/162042ByEvent.html Swimming: Men's 200m Individual Medley]. Published by Sports Illustrated. Retrieved 2013-06-13.</ref> [[Andorra at the 2008 Summer Olympics|2008]], [[Andorra at the 2012 Summer Olympics|2012]]<ref>[https://www.bbc.com/sport/olympics/2012/athletes/8f2414b9-2b5f-4b34-8f5f-b0725c7caee5 Hocine Haciane Constantin's entry] from the [[BBC]]'s London 2013 coverage. Updated 2012-08-13. Retrieved 2013-06-13.</ref>
*World Championships:2003, 2005, 2009, [[Andorra at the 2011 World Aquatics Championships|2011]]
*Mediterranean Games: [[Andorra at the 2009 Mediterranean Games|2009]]
*[[Games of the Small States of Europe|GSSE]]: 2001, 2003, 2005, 2007, 2009, 2011
*Short Course Worlds: 2010
